chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the mosque which was 'founded on piety' (tasiisa 'ala al-taqwa), and he said, 'The Mosque of Quba'.
ai.seo_question: Which mosque is referred to as the one 'founded on piety' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explicitly identifies the 'Mosque founded on piety' (Masjid al-Taqwa) mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah as the Mosque of Quba, the first mosque built by the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) upon his arrival in Medina. This hadith serves as a crucial exegetical link (tafsir) between the Quranic verse and the historical reality of early Islamic practice, emphasizing the virtue of establishing places of worship grounded in taqwa (God-consciousness) and community cohesion.
